name: WineEngine
motto: Everyone can be a game developer.
tagline: Ask in a chat and the AI drives the engine to build it. Because it is connected over MCP, an AI in the ChatGPT or Claude desktop app can operate the engine directly.
concepts: Anyone can make a game with AI
Data is kept in a form AI can handle
Suited to short development like game jams
summary:
A C++20 game engine that renders with DxLib, plus an editor modeled on Unity (started on Aug 9, 2026).
Every editor operation is exposed as a "command", and the GUI, command palette, headless CLI and MCP all go through the same path, so an AI as well as a person can drive the editor from the outside.

steps.label: STEP 1
steps.title: Ask in words
steps.caption: Just write "make a small garden with a house, a tree and a pond". No file names or commands needed
steps.prompt: Make a small garden with a house, a tree and a pond.

steps.label: STEP 2
steps.title: The AI operates the editor
steps.caption: When the AI builds a scene, before and after pictures appear side by side. A person reviews and approves the changes before they stay

steps.label: STEP 3
steps.title: Everything it did is kept
steps.caption: How much time went to which kind of work is recorded as a graph and counts

history.title: Every command the AI used is kept: when, and what it did
history.caption: The history of commands the AI actually called over MCP (scene.apply, scene.save and more)

shared.title: Handed out and in use
shared.body: The engine itself is given to other people, who connect it from ChatGPT / Claude and make games with it. "Anyone can make a game with AI" now works in practice.

figures.caption: The editor right after the AI built a scene: new Entities in the Hierarchy and the result shown at once in Scene and Game. AI Activity sits next to the Inspector

pillars.title: An editor modeled on Unity
pillars.body: Scene, Game, Hierarchy and Inspector, Keep Changes to retain edits made during Play, and dragging assets onto the Inspector, so Unity habits carry over.

pillars.title: Semantic scene diffs
pillars.body: Shows "which Entity changed what", which git diff cannot. A Git client and an integrated terminal are built into the editor.

pillars.title: From design doc to exe and iOS
pillars.body: Compose screens, write behavior in C++ and export, all with the same commands. Besides a Windows exe, it supports iOS (build on a Mac and submit to the App Store).

pillars.title: The tools are inside
pillars.body: Effects, sound, drawing, timeline, Live2D-style 2D characters, terrain, physics and enemy AI: the tools a game needs live inside the engine.
